note: Canonical merge contract for Solutions progress. This file is the single source: docs-site tests/fixtures/solutions-progress-merge.json and docs-ui tests/solution-progress/fixtures/merge-vectors.json are byte-identical copies. Edit here, copy verbatim; both test suites run every vector.
rules: Document shape: {v:1, updatedAt, solutions:{<id>:{completedSteps[], currentStep, startedAt, updatedAt, completedAt, solutionVersion}}}. Timestamps are epoch milliseconds (numbers) on the wire and in storage; ISO 8601 strings are accepted on input and normalized to numbers.
Each vector is merge(existing, incoming) evaluated at clock `now`. docs-site calls mergeAll(stored, clientBody); docs-ui calls merge(remote, local), so its local copy is `incoming`.

Normalization before merging: solution ids and step ids must match /^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,62}[a-z0-9])?$/ (invalid step ids dropped); completedSteps deduplicated in first-seen order and capped at the last 100; currentStep must be a valid step id else null; solutionVersion must match /^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/ else null; unusable timestamps become null, except updatedAt which becomes 0; unknown keys are dropped.
Clamp: any timestamp later than now + 5 minutes becomes now + 5 minutes.
Per solution: the record with the greater updatedAt is `later`, the other `earlier`. On a tie the incoming record is `later`.
completedSteps = earlier.completedSteps followed by the later record steps not already present (ordered union), capped at the last 100.
updatedAt = max(a.updatedAt, b.updatedAt). startedAt = min of the non-null values (null only when both are null).
currentStep = later.currentStep, falling back to earlier.currentStep when null. solutionVersion follows the same rule.

completedAt = the earliest non-null value when the two solutionVersions are equal or either is null; when both are set and differ, completedAt = null (the completion no longer applies to the current step list).
Solutions present on only one side are kept unchanged after normalization.
Document updatedAt = max(existing.updatedAt, incoming.updatedAt, every merged record updatedAt); 0 for an empty document.
After merging, keep at most 50 solutions, evicting the smallest updatedAt first (ties by id), then keep evicting until the serialized document is at most 32768 bytes.
The `invalid` cases are client bodies the strict validator rejects (HTTP 400). The stored side is read leniently: bad keys and records are dropped, the rest kept.

vectors.name: ordered union: earlier record order first, later record additions appended
merge is commutative: swapping existing and incoming gives the same document
timestamps: updatedAt is the max, startedAt the earliest non-null
completedAt: earliest non-null when both records carry the same version
version change clears completedAt and takes the later record version
version change clears completedAt even when the later record is the completed one
currentStep and solutionVersion come from the later record, falling back to the other when null
a tie on updatedAt lets the incoming record win currentStep
unknown keys are dropped at every level
timestamps ahead of now by more than 5 minutes are clamped to now + 5 minutes
invalid step ids are dropped and duplicates collapse, order preserved
an invalid currentStep or solutionVersion becomes null rather than failing the document
unusable timestamps: updatedAt becomes 0, the others null
solutions on only one side are kept unchanged; document updatedAt is the max of both
both sides empty produce an empty document with updatedAt 0
ISO 8601 inputs on both sides normalize to epoch milliseconds
an ISO stored document merges with a millisecond incoming one on the same clock
more than 50 solutions: the oldest by updatedAt are evicted
more than 100 completed steps: the earliest are dropped
